text:
natalie (support): Heads-up — customer on Dedicated (private VPC) reporting user API requests intermittently 401 when routed through their ALB -> Istio ingress -> our dedicated gateway. Works if we hit the gateway directly. They see variance across regions. Repro steps below.

natalie (support): Repro from their network (curl):
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDWOOD-KEY-xxxx' \\n  -H 'X-Request-ID: 7f3b-cust-1' \\n  'https://private-gw.customer.example/api/v1/generate'
```

natalie (support): Sometimes returns 200, sometimes 401 with body: `{\"error\":\"authentication failed\"}`. They see `x-forwarded-auth` header present on ALB but not on our gateway logs for failed requests.

tia (eng-infra): Can you grab raw tcp/http capture from the ALB -> istio sidecar for a failing and a succeeding request? Need to confirm if ALB is rewriting Authorization or setting cookie.

natalie (support): Got two pcap snippets from customer (attached link). Short logs: failing request shows ALB -> istio adds `x-amzn-oidc` and `x-forwarded-proto`, then Istio envoy removes `authorization` header before reaching our LB.

ashley (eng-platform): That header removal rings a bell — we've seen `envoy.filters.http.header_to_metadata` or `external_auth` policies strip headers when ext_authz configured. Are they using Istio's RequestAuthentication/authzpolicy?

mike (eng-security): Also check for cookie to bearer rewrites in their LB. Some SSO setups rewrite `Cookie` into `Authorization` at the edge and then drop it. If our gateway expects `Authorization: Bearer` and it disappears we return 401.

leo (eng-runtime): Quick triage on our side: our gateway logs show for the failing trace id `7f3b-cust-1` we received no Authorization header. We then try session lookup and fail. Here's snippet from gateway access log: `{\"time\":\"...\",\"req_id\":\"7f3b-cust-1\",\"auth_present\":false,\"upstream_status\":401}`

natalie (support): Customer's Istio config excerpt (they shared):
```yaml
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: RequestAuthentication
metadata:
  name: allow-jwt
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: edge
  jwtRules:
  - issuer: "https://idp.example/"
  - jwksUri: "https://idp.example/.well-known/jwks.json"
---
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: rewrite-policy
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: edge
  action: CUSTOM
  rules:
  - to:
    - operation:
        methods: ["POST"]
    when:
    - key: request.headers["Authorization"]
      values: ["*"]
```

tia (eng-infra): That `CUSTOM` action is suspicious — they might have an ext_authz webhook that rewrites headers. If ext_authz responds without `allowed_headers` include, envoy will drop. Need ext_authz config.

mike (eng-security): Request customer to paste their Envoy ext_authz config or the webhook logs. Ask them if ext_authz returns a 200 with `headers_to_add` or `headers_to_remove`.

natalie (support): Asked customer for ext_authz logs. They responded: ext_authz returns 200 and adds `x-user-claim: bob@example.com`, then returns `status: HTTP_OK`. No explicit `headers_to_add` for Authorization. They say they used an old proxy that intentionally removes Authorization to avoid leaking internal tokens.

ashley (eng-platform): If the client's ingress intentionally removes Authorization, we need them to either forward a signed header (e.g., x-rw-forward-auth: <signed token>) or configure their ext_authz to whitelist `authorization` as allowed to upstream. We can accept either.

leo (eng-runtime): Workaround for customer: have their ALB add a signed X-Forwarded-Authorization header that our gateway validates (we have an option in dedicated gateway `allow_forwarded_auth: true` when customer signs with a registered key). I can enable a short-lived toggle for their deployment to test.

mike (eng-security): Before toggling, we should confirm the forwarding scheme: we only accept forwarded auth when HMAC signed and expiry < 60s. Send spec for the signed header.

leo (eng-runtime): Spec snippet I can share to customer now:
```
X-Forwarded-Authorization: hmacv1 t=..., k=key-id, s=signature, e=expiry
```
We validate `k` against customer keys and `s` HMAC over (method,path,t,expiry).

natalie (support): Customer says they can add that header on ALB Lambda@Edge. They're nervous about SSO user tokens though — they prefer our gateway to accept JWT forwarded claims instead of raw token.

ashley (eng-platform): We can accept `x-forwarded-user-jwt` with same signing if customer can craft one. But that requires we map to internal session; need eng-runtime to confirm mapping rules.

leo (eng-runtime): Mapping rules: if header `x-forwarded-user-jwt` present and signature valid, we extract `sub`/`scope` claims and mint an internal short-lived api-session bound to that request id. We can provisionally enable for this customer.

tia (eng-infra): I'll coordinate a test window. Natalie, please propose a 30-min window and ask them to provide a failing request example and the same request with the forwarded header added. We'll capture traces.

natalie (support): Scheduled 2026-03-18 17:00 UTC test window. Customer will add the signed header for the test.

mike (eng-security): I'll review the signing docs and approve keys for that account before we enable `allow_forwarded_auth`. Security checklist: key rotation policy, minimum expiry 10s, audit log enabled.

leo (eng-runtime): Once enabled, I'll watch `auth_forward` metrics and specific req_id. I'll also add extra logging for `auth_source` so we can confirm it changed from `none` to `forwarded`.

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: enable-feature allow_forwarded_auth for customer-corp-dedicated at 2026-03-18T16:55:00Z (rolling, no downtime).

natalie (support): Thanks everyone — I'll own coordination with the customer and post results in this thread. If the workaround succeeds we'll add a KB article describing how to configure ALB/Istio ext_authz to preserve/forward auth to Redwood gateway.

ashley (eng-platform): If customer refuses forwarded auth, we should document the permanent recommendation: terminate auth at our gateway (direct TLS) or use internal proxy that preserves Authorization header.

mike (eng-security): Agreed. We'll follow up with a secure spec and onboarding doc after test.

natalie (support): Update after test: customer applied signed header. During the window we saw 10 requests — 9 succeeded with forwarded auth; 1 failed because expiry was 5s and we dropped it. Customer updated expiry to 30s and all green. We'll keep feature on. Closing after KB drafted.
